question.problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{′}+3y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $4$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+{{field-2}}\cdot sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})
$$
question.worked_solution:
We assume that a solution of our equation has the following Fourier series:

$$
{y}_{p}∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+{b}_{n}sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+{b}_{n}sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})) \\  & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\cdot (-\frac{n\pi }{2}sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))+{b}_{n}\cdot \frac{n\pi }{2}cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\  & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{2}sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{p}^{′}$ and ${y}_{p}$ into the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{2}sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})) \\  & \,+3(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+{b}_{n}sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})) \\  & \,\,={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned} & \frac{3{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}+3{a}_{n})cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\  & \,\,+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{2}+3{b}_{n})sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\  & \,\,\,\,={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, equating the free terms and the cosine and sine coefficients, we obtain the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3{a}_{0}}{2}=0 \\ \frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}+3{a}_{n}=0 \\ -\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{2}+3{b}_{n}=\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, ${a}_{0}=0.$ 

Next, from the second equation, 

$$
{a}_{n}=-\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{6}.
$$

Substituting this into the third equation gives

$$
-(-\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{6})\frac{n\pi }{2}+3{b}_{n}=\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }\,⇒\,{b}_{n}=\frac{24(-1)^{n}}{n\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+36)}
$$

Therefore, for ${a}_{n}$ with $n\ge 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{6} \\  & =-\frac{n\pi }{6}\cdot \frac{24(-1)^{n}}{n\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+36)} \\  & =-\frac{4(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+36}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,-\frac{4(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+36}\cdot cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+\frac{24(-1)^{n}}{n\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+36)}\cdot sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$
